summary: Count substrings of a string over {a,b,c} that contain at least one of each character.
mainInsight: Once a window [l, r] contains all three characters, every extension to the right (r..n-1) also does, so add n - r and then shrink from the left. Equivalent: for each right end the number of valid starts is min(last a, last b, last c) + 1.

approaches.name: Sliding window
approaches.summary: When valid, add n - r; shrink from the left.

approaches.name: Last-seen indices
approaches.summary: ans += min(last[a], last[b], last[c]) + 1 for each r.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal; the last-seen-index version is a one-line alternative.

promptVariants: Which pattern counts substrings containing all of a set of characters?
What is the key idea for counting (not maximising) with a window?
options: Sliding window counting extensions to the right
Dynamic programming over every start/end substring pair
A trie of all the substrings of the string
Binary search on the substring length with a check
cards.answer: Sliding window counting extensions to the right
cards.explanation: Each minimal valid left boundary contributes n - r substrings.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Binary search on the substring length wi: Counting needs every valid substring, not just a length.

promptVariants: Why add `len(s) - r` when the window [l, r] is valid?
How does shrinking from the left then count the other substrings?
cards.answer: If [l, r] contains a, b and c, every substring [l, r'] with r' >= r also does: n - r of them. Then removing s[l] and moving l forward counts the valid substrings starting at later left positions on subsequent steps while the window remains valid.
keyPoints: Extensions to the right stay valid
n - r substrings per valid left
Shrink to count the next left
cards.explanation: Counting by left boundary avoids double counting.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Extra space (three counters): ___
Why is the answer incremented inside the while loop and what does `freq[s[l]] -= 1` do to the next iteration?
What is the invariant after the while loop ends?
cards.answer: Each iteration of the while loop corresponds to a distinct valid left boundary l (with right end r): it adds n - r substrings, then removes s[l] and checks the next left boundary. After the loop the window [l, r] no longer contains all three, so no further left boundary is valid for this r.
keyPoints: One iteration per valid left boundary
cards.explanation: Equivalent to counting min(last_a, last_b, last_c) + 1 per r.

promptVariants: How many substrings contain a, b and c?

incorrectOptionExplanations.1: More than the single 'abc' qualify: extending it by a or c keeps all three.
incorrectOptionExplanations.6: Six would also count substrings that miss one of the letters.
